primary_result: Bounded residual learning markedly improves RAW over prior direct action readout, but does not establish positive RAW geometry/action generalization over the fixed state baseline.

raw.interpretation: Training fit and the reserved validation episode improve, but Normal historical holdout worsens. Optimizing longer past512 does not improve validation selection. This supports remaining generalization/validation-coverage limitations, not an isolated encoder design defect.
raw.partial_benefits: RAW improves mean Over joint error and Normal gripper MAE, while Normal full-block joint RMS and normalized14 MSE worsen; benefit is not uniform across targets/scenes

native.interpretation: Small positive Normal increment beyond matched nominal state-residual control. Only3 Normal heldout episodes, two seeds; no statistical population or robustness claim.

selection: Only validation normalized14 MSE chooses checkpoint/gate, full50-step action supervision. All6 selected gates1; zero candidate retained but not selected. Validation fallback did not protect RAW Normal holdout. No test-driven gate override.
regression: RAW selected steps256/384 remain unchanged at512/1024 budgets. Native selected1024/704. Last weights retained; cosine3e-4 to3e-5 reduced previous gross fitting regression; no assumption of monotonic generalization.
recommended_next: Do not lengthen RAW residual training on this split just to force a positive result. Before joint encoder updates, strengthen episode-level validation coverage (predeclare leave-one-training-episode-out if retaining5 demonstrations) and inspect scene/phase-specific residual errors, then compare residual objective with limited task-supervised encoder adaptation under the same baseline. Keep historical test identity and no test-based tuning.
